meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/01, Thursday 16 May 2024). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: The download folder these came from was labelled Nov 24, but the papers are the SUMMER 2024 series: J560/01 is dated Thursday 16 May 2024, /02 Monday 3 June 2024 and /03 Monday 10 June 2024. Filed as JUN24 on the papers' own printed dates. As with the June 2025 OCR papers there is no per-question total printed — only a bare [N] against each part — so the whole-paper sum against the published 100 is the only check available, and this file passes it. Coded WITH mark_split, unlike the six OCR June 2025 papers; see coding_notes for what OCR's notation does and does not give.

coding_notes: mark_split for OCR is DERIVED, not transcribed. OCR prints a single part total and then the partial-credit routes ('3' with 'M2 for … or M1 for …'), so the split recorded here is the method/accuracy structure those routes imply — for that example, 'M2 A1'. It is reliable for sizing method marks against answer marks, which is what lib/exam/markEvidence.data.ts uses it for, but it is not a quotation of an Edexcel-style code string.
q1d (a prime number less than 10) tagged factors_and_multiples rather than prime_factor_decomposition — recognising a prime is not decomposing a number into primes.

q3b (explain from three angles that a triangle is isosceles) tagged properties_of_2d_shapes. The mark scheme explicitly refuses answers that argue from sides, so the claim being tested is knowing which property defines the shape.
q5 (subtract then divide, given the result) tagged solving_linear_equations, not function_machines: no machine is drawn, and the item is worded as a number the student must recover.

q6b (the fraction of a list of combinations that include one item) tagged systematic_listing. Forming a fraction from a context is a documented taxonomy gap — every fraction node covers operating on a fraction, not writing one down — and the mark scheme follows through from the candidate's own list, so the list is what is being credited.
q14 (production rate over 7 hours) tagged proportion then time_calculations: the scaling is a unit rate and one mark's worth of the work is the hours-to-minutes conversion.
q17 tagged fractional_enlargements — the scale factor is ½.
q23 tagged upper_and_lower_bounds, matching OCR-JUN25-F-P3 q24b, which is the same 'show it may not fit' comparison of two error intervals.
